summary: Handle JavaScript constructors that explicitly return an object which replaces the newly allocated instance.

target.notes: Use the JavaScript-compatible construction path because C# instance constructors cannot return a replacement object.

semantics.base_constructor_object_return: replacement object becomes result of new

caveats: Do not simulate this by factory conversion unless every `new`/subclassing/identity interaction is also rewritten consistently.

tests.name: base constructor returns object
tests.input: class C { constructor() { this.x = 1; return {x: 2}; } } console.log(new C().x);

tests.name: edge: base constructor primitive return ignored
tests.input: class C { constructor() { this.x = 1; return 5; } } console.log(new C().x);
